# Dear ImGui's ImRound64() casts to an integer before checking the value, so a non-finite window
# coordinate from the docking layout trips UBSan inside the framework. HDRView passes no NaN of its own
# down that path -- the whole reported stack is ImGui and hello_imgui -- and the helper's own source
# comments the limitation ("FIXME: Positive values only.").
float-cast-overflow:imgui_internal.h
float-cast-overflow:implot_internal.h

# stb_image_write's JPEG encoder accumulates its bit buffer in a signed int and shifts it left once it
# has gone negative (stbiw__jpg_writeBits, "bitBuf <<= 8"), which is undefined before C++20 though it is
# what every two's-complement target does anyway. The whole reported stack is stb's, HDRView only hands
# it pixels, and the file is vendored -- so it is suppressed rather than patched.
shift-base:stb_image_write.h

# libheif's StreamReader_memory::read() does memcpy(dst, &m_data[m_position], size), and taking that
# address on an empty buffer yields a null pointer that memcpy is declared never to accept -- even when
# size is zero and nothing is copied. Reported inside libheif on files HDRView only hands it bytes for.
nonnull-attribute:bitstream.cc

# stb_image_resize2's scratch buffer is carved into pieces whose 64-bit header stores land wherever the
# preceding piece ended (stbir__perform_build), so a reduction to certain sizes writes a stbir_uint64 at a
# four-byte boundary. Undefined by the language, permitted by every target HDRView builds for, and the
# whole reported stack is stb's -- HDRView hands it a float buffer and a size. Reached from
# Image::resample(), so from resizing an image and from every level of a generated mip pyramid.
alignment:stb_image_resize2.h
